title: "What Are We?", Played Twice
old_caption:
Asking "what are we" the bad way, then the better way.
Lead with "I like you" and leave room for their answer. Watch till the verdict.

title: What's an aspect in astrology?
old_caption:
Lines all over your chart can feel like a puzzle. Astrologers read aspects as conversations between planets: some easy, some tense, most a bit of both.
Just like the people you love.

title: What's an attachment style?
old_caption: Attachment styles describe how we reach for closeness and safety. They're a pattern, not a label for a whole person. And with steady, safe people, styles can grow.

title: What is a birth chart?
old_caption:
A birth chart is a map of the sky from the place and minute you were born. Astrologers read it like a story, not a single sentence.
Think of it as your very first sky.

title: What's a boundary, really?
old_caption:
A boundary isn't a rule for someone else. It's what you will do, like stepping out of a yelling match and talking later.
Said kindly and clearly, it's a gift to both of you. Boundaries are doors, not walls.

title: What's a composite chart?
old_caption: A composite chart isn't yours or theirs. It blends both into one chart for the relationship itself. A sweet reminder that the "us" is something you both get to tend.

title: What does enthusiastic consent mean?
old_caption:
Enthusiastic consent means a clear yes, freely given. A yes can become a no at any time, so check in and keep checking in.
"Um, I guess?" isn't a yes. Only yes means yes.

title: Why do astrologers love eclipses?
old_caption:
An eclipse is the Sun, Moon and Earth lining up, and astrologers read it as a turning point or a new chapter.
A gentle reminder: never look at the Sun without proper eclipse glasses.

title: Fire, earth, air, water: which are you?
old_caption:
Fire, earth, air or water? Each element holds three signs, and most charts mix several.
You're not just one ingredient. You're a whole kitchen, and that's a lovely thing to be.

title: How do you say how you feel?
old_caption: Going quiet and hoping they'll guess rarely works. Try this frame: "I feel ___ when ___. I need ___." Simple, honest and kind. Save it for the next hard talk.
